item.title: Binance to resume withdrawals after covering bulk of stolen $6.3 billion
item.description: Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals on Sunday after covering 95% of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in the world's largest ...
item.content:encoded:
Binance to resume withdrawals after covering bulk of stolen $6.3 billion Reuters | Updated: 01-11-2026 11:27 IST | Created: 01-11-2026 11:27 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals on Sunday after covering 95% of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in the world's largest digital heist, which the FBI has tied to North Korea. The exchange, founded in China, said the first phase of withdrawals would start between 0600 and 0900 GMT and cover 15 cryptoassets including bitcoin, ether, XRP, dogecoin and others. Binance said on Sunday it had covered $6 billion of stolen cryptocurrencies by using company money to buy replacement tokens. The remaining 5% of stolen tokens consist of assets that are less liquid and may take longer to source in the required amounts, according to the exchange. FBI TIES ATTACK TO NORTH KOREAN UNIT The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. The FBI said on Saturday the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack. Pyongyang has for years denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment. Law enforcement observed members of the unit converting stolen assets into the cryptocurrency ether, the FBI said in a statement, adding that it expected "further laundering" of the assets through the use of related technology. Analysts had blamed North Korea and said the Binance theft could be the largest financial heist of all time. The bulk of the theft unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. US President Donald Trump, however, said on Saturday that the US was still not certain if North Korea was involved. "We don't know if it's North Korea — but if it is, we'll talk to North Korea about it," Trump told reporters on Saturday in comments posted by a White House handle on X. BINANCE VOWS TO BEAR FINANCIAL COSTS Binance has been working with industry partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located as of Friday, it said. The exchange has repeatedly said it would bear the financial impact of the funds stolen in the hack. It has set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The money spent buying replacement tokens came from Binance's $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users( SAFU), a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some of its Futures Insurance Fund and its corporate treasury, it said on X. Co-CEO Yi He said on Saturday that 50% of its SAFU funds would be used, while the company committed to replenishing the fund to about $1 billion. Richard Teng, the other co-CEO, has said that the breach was a "complex attack" involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it harder to trace and investigate. Crypto prices fell on Friday, while Binance sought to reassure customers that their funds were safe after the hack. Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.

item.title: India, Turkey proposing ideas for passage of grain shipments in Black Sea: Marco Rubio
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday stated India and Turkey have proposed ideas for vessels carrying grain to pass the Black Sea amid strikes in the wake of the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.
item.content:encoded:
India, Turkey proposing ideas for passage of grain shipments in Black Sea: Marco Rubio US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday stated India and Turkey have proposed ideas for vessels carrying grain to pass the Black Sea amid strikes in the wake of the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 23:09 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 23:09 IST

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Saturday stated India and Turkey have proposed ideas for vessels carrying grain to pass the Black Sea amid strikes in the wake of the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. As Rubio hosted the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, speaking to the press, he said that passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz is even more challenging. He noted that the US has received limited cooperation in Hormuz despite President Donald Trump’s call to join Washington’s efforts in the region. Rubio said, “When you talk about the Black Sea, you saw a lot of countries speak up and express their willingness to contribute. Both Turkey and India have come to the table with some ideas about how we can get grain shipments moving because this is threatening global food security and, to some extent, energy security as well.” “In the case of the Strait of Hormuz, it's more challenging, because many countries around the world don't have the ability to project power in the region. The President has repeatedly asked countries to join us in the effort to protect global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. So far, we've had very limited cooperation, but not much. The responsibility has primarily fallen on the United States to protect shipping,” he added. Further, he also took note of territorial claims on waterways in the Indo-Pacific region as a maritime challenge in the region. He said, “Obviously, in the Indo-Pacific, we don't have active kinetic operations taking place like those we're seeing in the Strait of Hormuz or even in the Black Sea. But we do face some challenges, including territorial claims that we do not recognise. That's why you see us not only maintaining a presence in that part of the world but also operating jointly and cooperatively with our partners to continue making it clear that we do not accept illegitimate territorial claims over waterways that are either international waters or not the territorial waters of any single nation.” US and Iran have exchanged strikes amid a “blockade” in the strategic waterways of the Strait of Hormuz. While Iran continues to strike commercial vehicles, the United States reportedly struck two fishing boats off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, injuring two Iranian fishermen. As reported by the news agency IRNA, the two fishermen who went missing after the drone attack have been found, according to the CEO of the Qeshm Fishing Community. Both were sent back to Qeshm Island. Meanwhile, one of the two injured fishermen was taken to a hospital, Al Jazeera reported, citing Fars news agency. Meanwhile, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan noted that the situation in the Black Sea is on the agenda for the meeting between Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Even the Quad Foreign Ministers on Saturday called for preserving navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait against the backdrop of tensions in West Asia. (ANI)

item.title: Iran's FM Araghchi welcomes JD Vance's letter as "positive step"; says not ruling out possibility of “outbreak of war”
item.description: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday welcomed the peace talks with the United States as he received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, while noting that Iran has not ruled out the ...
item.content:encoded:
Iran's FM Araghchi welcomes JD Vance's letter as "positive step"; says not ruling out possibility of “outbreak of war” Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday welcomed the peace talks with the United States as he received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, while noting that Iran has not ruled out the possibility of an “outbreak of war.” ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 21:37 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 21:37 IST

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday welcomed the peace talks with the United States as he received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, while noting that Iran has not ruled out the possibility of an “outbreak of war.” In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi said, “The American side’s attempt to open the door to dialogue and understanding more broadly is a positive step.” However, he added, “If Washington’s goal in sending this letter is to stir up discord, it would be yet another mistake to add to its previous ones.” The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent the letter to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei on the instructions of US President Donald Trump, seeking to restart negotiations and prevent further US military strikes. As the possibility of fresh strikes lurks in Iran, the Minister said, “We do not rule out any possibility regarding the outbreak of war, and we are prepared for all scenarios. We have upgraded our weaponry, addressed our vulnerabilities, and tested new arms; our forces are at the highest level of readiness.” An American delegation is expected to join Iranian officials for talks in Doha; he said that Qatar has proposed to reduce the implementation period of Iran’s plan to open the strategic waterway, Strait of Hormuz, to two days as compared to five. Araghchi told Al Jazeera, “The Qatari side proposed shortening the implementation period of the Iranian proposal to five days. We have reached a proposal at this stage that reduces the implementation period to two days.” “Our conditions include lifting the sanctions imposed following the Islamabad memorandum and reducing US forces in the region. We demand the restoration of oil waivers and the release of all our frozen funds, including those held in Qatar. Reopening the Strait of Hormuz in accordance with our conditions paves the way for the resumption of negotiations with Washington regarding outstanding issues,” he added. An American delegation is likely to join Iranian officials for direct talks in Doha following a reported breakthrough in indirect negotiations, The Times of Israel reported, citing the Qatari newspaper Al-Araby Al-Jadeed. According to the report, citing sources close to mediation efforts, the two sides have reached an understanding on preliminary measures concerning Iran's nuclear programme, navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and financial incentives for Tehran. China and Russia are also reportedly expected to serve as guarantors of any agreement. However, Iran’s armed forces chief of staff, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, as per Al Jazeera, has said that Iran will respond to any attack with “immense force.” The Iranian armed forces chief’s remark echoed Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei order to confront all the threats “with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response.” According to a series of X posts by the account of Mojtaba Khamenei, the Iranian leader met with senior commanders of the armed forces against the backdrop of possibilities of fresh escalation between the United States and Iran. “Every level and type of threat must be confronted with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response,” the statement read. In a strongly worded statement, he instructed the armed forces to retaliate in case the military attacks resume. “If the enemies resume military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the people of Iran who will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” he said. Earlier, US President Trump stated that Washington is in no hurry to end its war with Iran, characterising the ongoing hostilities as "not a typical war" while maintaining that time favours the American side despite months of fighting and repeated diplomatic efforts failing to yield a lasting settlement. (ANI)

item.description: As reported by the news agency IRNA, the two fishermen who went missing after the drone attack have been found, according to the CEO of the Qeshm Fishing Community. Both were sent back to Qeshm Island ...
item.content:encoded:
Iran claims US struck fishing boats off Qeshm Island, two injured As reported by the news agency IRNA, the two fishermen who went missing after the drone attack have been found, according to the CEO of the Qeshm Fishing Community. Both were sent back to Qeshm Island. ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 18:39 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 18:39 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States reportedly struck two fishing boats off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, injuring two Iranian fishermen. As reported by the news agency IRNA, the two fishermen who went missing after the drone attack have been found, according to the CEO of the Qeshm Fishing Community. Both were sent back to Qeshm Island. Meanwhile, one of the two injured fishermen was taken to a hospital, Al Jazeera reported, citing Fars news agency. “This incident occurred around 11:30 am today involving two fishing boats within 18 miles of the village of Musan, affiliated with Qeshm County… Each boat had two occupants,” the deputy governor of Hormozgan Province for political, security, and social affairs told Tasnim news agency, as per Al Jazeera. As strikes continue in the Strait of Hormuz, earlier, Iranian naval forces destroyed an "enemy submarine" and damaged two commercial oil tankers in the operational zone east of Hormuz on Friday morning. State media Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) reported, citing the Iranian Navy's Public Relations department, that Iranian forces targeted and destroyed an adversary submarine navigating the operational sector near the vital maritime choke point. "This morning, an enemy submarine that was operating in the operational area east of the Strait of Hormuz was hit and destroyed by Iranian Navy sailors," the Navy statement read. Meanwhile, the Commander of the United States Central Command (CENTCOM), Admiral Brad Cooper, on Friday (local time) stated that the primary internationally recognised transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz have been successfully cleared of Iranian sea mines and commercial vessels are sailing freely through the strategic waterway. "Earlier this week, I visited some of the more than 50,000 service members supporting operations across the Middle East, including our mission in the Strait of Hormuz. When I flew over the strait, I saw dozens of commercial vessels transiting—all types: cargo, crude oil, liquid natural gas, or LNG. And I also saw our U.S. assets in the air and on the water, including a squadron of advanced sea drones that were on patrol, supporting a defensive layer," Admiral Cooper stated. This comes as the possibility of fresh strikes lurks in Iran. Today, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered senior commanders to confront all the threats “with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response.” According to a series of X posts by the account of Mojtaba Khamenei, the Iranian leader met with senior commanders of the armed forces against the backdrop of possibilities of fresh escalation between the United States and Iran. “Every level and type of threat must be confronted with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response,” the statement read. (ANI)
